identity.title: Third heart sound (S3 gallop) at apex with bell, left lateral decubitus

technique.how: Place the bell lightly over the apex with the patient in left lateral decubitus, in a quiet room, at end-expiration. Listen for a low-pitched dull sound 0.12-0.18 s after S2 (early diastole) giving a 'Ken-tuck-y' cadence; a right-sided S3 is heard at the lower left sternal border and increases with inspiration.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet environment, bell with light pressure, patient rolled to the left; time the sound against the carotid pulse.

interpretation.positive_finding: In dyspneic ED adults an audible S3 gallop is the single most rule-in physical sign for heart failure (pooled LR+ 11 in the RCE, 4.0 in a later meta-analysis) and is highly specific for elevated LVEDP or reduced LVEF. In acute MI it marks LV dysfunction and worse prognosis.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of an S3 barely changes the probability of heart failure (sensitivity ~11-50%), so a negative examination must not be used to rule out HF.
interpretation.pitfalls: A physiologic S3 is normal in children, young adults, athletes and pregnancy. Easily missed with the diaphragm, in obesity, COPD, tachycardia (summation gallop) or a noisy ward; can be confused with split S2, opening snap or pericardial knock.
interpretation.changes_what: Present S3 strongly raises probability of acute HF/cardiogenic cause and supports diuresis and echo; absent S3 does not lower it.

sources.citation: Wang CS, FitzGerald JM, Schulzer M, Mak E, Ayas NT. Does this dyspneic patient in the emergency department have congestive heart failure? JAMA 2005;294(15):1944-56.
Martindale JL, Wakai A, Collins SP, et al. Diagnosing acute heart failure in the emergency department: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med 2016;23(3):223-42.
Marcus GM, Gerber IL, McKeown BH, et al. Association between phonocardiographic third and fourth heart sounds and objective measures of left ventricular function. JAMA 2005;293(18):2238-44.

Mant J, Doust J, Roalfe A, et al. Systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis of diagnosis of heart failure, with modelling of implications of different diagnostic strategies in primary care. Health Technol Assess 2009;13(32):1-207.
Signs and symptoms in adult patients with acute dyspnea: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Emerg Med 2018;25(1):3-11 (author list not retrievable via abstract tool; confirmed by PMID/DOI).
Badgett RG, Lucey CR, Mulrow CD. Can the clinical examination diagnose left-sided heart failure in adults? JAMA 1997;277(21):1712-9.

estimates.target_condition: Congestive heart failure as cause of dyspnea
estimates.population: Adult ED patients presenting with dyspnea; 22 studies pooled in RCE
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical/echo-based HF diagnosis per included studies
estimates.quote: the sign of the third heart sound (S(3)) gallop (positive LR = 11; 95% CI, 4.9-25.0)

estimates.target_condition: Acute heart failure as cause of dyspnea
estimates.population: Adult ED patients with undifferentiated dyspnea; AHF prevalence 29-79% across included studies
estimates.reference_standard: Criterion standard = clinical data plus objective test results
estimates.quote: the auscultation of S3 on physical examination (4.0, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 2.7 to 5.9)

estimates.population: 90 adults undergoing elective left heart catheterization at a US teaching hospital; S3 detected by computerized phonocardiography (not auscultation)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.41/(1-0.92) = 5.1; LR- = (1-0.41)/0.92 = 0.64; specificity from abstract: 'the specificities of the S3 were 92%, 87%, and 92%'
estimates.quote: The sensitivities of these heart sounds to detect an elevated LVEDP, reduced LVEF, or elevated BNP were 41%, 52%, and 32% for an S3

estimates.population: Same 90-patient elective catheterization cohort; phonocardiographic S3
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.52/(1-0.87) = 4.0; LR- = (1-0.52)/0.87 = 0.55; sensitivity from abstract: 'were 41%, 52%, and 32% for an S3'
estimates.quote: the specificities of the S3 were 92%, 87%, and 92%

estimates.target_condition: Heart failure (new diagnosis) in primary care; index finding 'added heart sounds'
estimates.population: Patients with suspected heart failure in primary care; IPD meta-analysis of 9 studies
estimates.reference_standard: Echocardiography / expert panel per included studies
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.11/(1-0.99) = 11 (imprecise: specificity rounded to 99%); LR- = (1-0.11)/0.99 = 0.90; sensitivity quote: 'ranging from 11% (added heart sounds) to 53% (oedema)'
estimates.quote: orthopnoea (89%), oedema (72%), elevated jugular venous pressure (70%), cardiomegaly (85%), added heart sounds (99%), lung crepitations (81%)

estimates.target_condition: Heart failure as cause of acute dyspnea
estimates.population: Adults with a new episode of acute dyspnea; 8 ED studies, 4737 patients
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis of HF per included studies
estimates.quote: Elevated jugular venous pressure (0.88, pooled odds ratio: 7), added third heart sound (0.97), and lung crepitations (0.77, pooled odds ratio: 11)

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not rely on absence of S3 to exclude heart failure, or on presence of S3 in a young/pregnant patient to diagnose it.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: New S3 with chest pain or hypotension indicates significant LV dysfunction (possible MI/cardiogenic shock) and warrants urgent ECG, troponin and echo.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Interobserver agreement for S3 is poor to fair among clinicians; experienced listeners detect it more often (Badgett RCE; Marcus 2005 used phonocardiography as criterion standard).

extraction_notes: Wang 2005 abstract LR+ 11 is the primary estimate; Martindale 2016 pooled a different study set with lower LR+ 4.0, so both are entered separately rather than averaged. Marcus 2005 uses computerized phonocardiographic S3, which is more sensitive than bedside auscultation; LRs computed from rounded sens/spec without CIs. Mant 2009 'added heart sounds' includes S3/S4; LR+ from 99% specificity is numerically unstable. Badgett 1997 abstract has no numbers; cited for interobserver context. Wang's LR- for S3 (~0.88) is in the table only and not entered.
